cards.headline: A 1981 collaboration with Adrian Belew and Robin Scott
cards.snippet: In 1981, Japanese musician Ryuichi Sakamoto teamed up with guitarist Adrian Belew, who had played with Talking Heads and King Crimson, and with Robin Scott. Together they made an album called Left-Handed Dream. The Baffler described it as mixing slow, simmering, primeval techno with raw-edged sci-fi gagaku, using traditional Japanese taiko drums. This is not the Talking Heads song of the same name as the track you're hearing.
cards.context: Not to be confused with the Talking Heads song of the same name.

cards.headline: Fire-breathers in Amsterdam, but he only heard this
cards.snippet: I turned a corner and there were street performers all over a square, acrobats flipping in the air, men swallowing torches, belching fire, but the only thing I heard was this.
cards.context: A vivid memory of the song drowning out a chaotic street scene; the commenter also notes Sakamoto reportedly disliked working with Robin Scott on the LP.

cards.headline: Four words for Belew's guitar

cards.context: Belew's guitar on the track is known for its animal-like squawks and effects.

cards.headline: The marimba had its art-pop moment
cards.snippet: Seems like the marimba enjoyed a period of popularity in the late 70's and early 80's with a certain type of 'art pop' musician. Peter Gabriel, Sakamoto, Japan, Tears for Fears.
cards.context: A sharp observation placing the track's marimba sound in an early-80s trend.
